sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Ownership and Cross-Border Sub-Licensing of Trademarks and Patents

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition; commercial matters governed by the French Commercial Code, Code de commerce)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–United States Income Tax Treaty (1994, as amended by the 2006 and 2009 Protocols)
France–China Income Tax Agreement of 30 May 1984, as amended (including the 2013 Protocol)
France–Singapore Income Tax Agreement of 9 September 2009
France–Hong Kong Income Tax Agreement of 21 October 2010
France–Germany Income Tax Treaty of 21 July 1959, as amended by the 2015 Protocol
EU Council Directive 2003/49/EC (Interest and Royalties Directive) as transposed into French internal law

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50, L.561-45, L.561-46 and R.561-1 to R.561-9 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), as amended by Ordonnance n°2020-115 of 12 February 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Law n°2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II Law); Articles L.123-1 et seq. and L.227-1 to L.227-30 of the Commercial Code; Decree n°2020-118 of 12 February 2020 on the beneficial ownership (UBO) register administered by the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); General Regulation of the Autorité des Marchés Financiers applicable to investment services

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation (or equivalent commercial extract) of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry of companies in the shareholder's country of origin (e.g., equivalent of the French RCS/Kbis)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (attestation de bonne standing) issued by the foreign corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or designated administrative authority of the foreign jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Register of directors and shareholders / certificate of incumbency evidencing legal representation authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, board of directors, or statutory auditor of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO identification dossier (passport copy, proof of residential address, and clearing house verification for each direct and indirect beneficial owner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the jurisdiction of residence of the beneficial owner; passport issued by the competent national authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization + Hague Apostille + certified French translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under Articles L.561-5 of the Monetary and Financial Code against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014), UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, the French national list of terrorist asset-freezing measures (FTO list), and OFAC SDN List for all USD-denominated wire transfers and correspondent banking exchanges via the Baviera system. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be screened per FATF Recommendation 12 and Article L.561-10; enhanced due diligence applies to medium-risk IP HoldCo structures sourcing royalty payments from multiple foreign jurisdictions, with mandatory suspicious transaction reporting to TRACFIN within 48 hours under Article L.561-15.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI); RCS availability database accessible via data.inpi.fr and Infogreffe.fr; trademark/name opposition checks performed through INPI's e-procedure.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Toubon Law (Law n°94-665 of 4 August 1994), the statutory name, articles of association, and all mandatory corporate filings presented to French authorities must be in French; a foreign-language corporate name is permissible only when accompanied by a French transliteration or official French equivalent. All corporate names must be in Latin script, may contain French diacritical marks, numerals, and abbreviations, and must not create confusion with existing RCS-registered entities or registered trademarks. Names of UBOs in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic) must be formally transliterated and, where required, accompanied by a certified translation for RCS registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France métropolitaine (where implying state authority or misleading geographic scope)
Sociétés agréées par l'AMF (unless the entity holds the corresponding licence)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not maintain a standalone pre-incorporation name reservation certificate; availability is tested during the Guichet Unique filing and final confirmation occurs upon RCS issuance of the Kbis. If the INPI/RCS registrar rejects the name on grounds of identity or confusing similarity, the applicant may (i) refile immediately through the Guichet Unique with a modified name, (ii) file an administrative challenge (recours gracieux) with the President of the Commercial Court (Tribunal de commerce) within 15 days of the refusal, (iii) initiate an opposition proceeding before INPI under the Intellectual Property Code (Article L.712-4, 2-month deadline), or (iv) lodge a judicial appeal before the competent civil court within 2 months of the rejection decision. Extension of the 30-day availability window is not statutorily permitted; refiling commences a new review cycle.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SAS must have a real registered office (siège social) within France; use of a virtual or domiciliation address is permitted exclusively via a licensed commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation agréée) for a maximum statutory term of 5 consecutive years, but for an IP HoldCo claiming patent box benefits under Article 238 of the General Tax Code and seeking treaty-reduced royalty withholding rates, an isolated virtual office materially increases substance erosion risk. The tax administration and URSSAF apply the EU ATAD/CFC and BEPS Action 5 nexus criteria; a physical office with substantive decision-making capacity, local management, and payroll substance is strongly advised.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-to-high: approximately 30% probability of an unannounced on-site physical inspection within the first three fiscal years if the entity claims the 10% patent box regime or treaty royalty benefits; approximately 10% for a standard passive IP HoldCo without preferential tax claims. Inspections are conducted by DGFiP (tax audit unit) and URSSAF, which have statutory powers of entry and document seizure without a court warrant under Articles L.16 B and L.80 F of the Book of Tax Procedures.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of articles of association (statuts), shareholder resolutions, bylaws for SAS, and corporate governance pack compliant with Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 of the Commercial Code
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal counsel (French avocat au barreau or notaire)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for structuring a Société par Actions Simplifiée with cross-border IP licensing provisions; no statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official registration fees via Guichet Unique: RCS immobilisation, droit fixe, and greffe du tribunal de commerce fees for creation of a commercial entity
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Decree n°2020-118 and the amended decree on administrative fees of 2016 (décret n°2016-230)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice (annonce légale) in a prefecture-approved legal gazette in France
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'annonces légales approved by the local Préfecture
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory ceiling per departmental prefectural order (varies by number of lines and department)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name availability and trademark pre-screening search (screening against INPI national trademark database, European Union Intellectual Property Office - EUIPO, and WIPO international registrations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee for trademark search and name analysis per Article L.712-1 of the Intellectual Property Code

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation, notarization, and apostille bundle for foreign UBO/corporate documents (share certificates, passport copies, certificates of incumbency, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-certified translator (traducteur expert) and Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs (Service de l'Apostille) or Notary Public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory translator tariffs and Hague Apostille fixed fee of 17 EUR per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / commercial domiciliation agreement with a licensed domiciliation company (first full year of service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; requires conformity with Article L.123-11-2 of the Commercial Code

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC compliance onboarding: UBO identification and verification, PEP/sanctions screening, risk-based due diligence file preparation for bank account opening and RCS UBO declaration filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Managed compliance services provider (external DPO/AML officer)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark aligned with Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 of the Monetary and Financial Code; UBO filing fee to RCS is €25

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, including Articles L. 210-1 et seq. (commercial companies), L. 227-1 et seq. (SAS), L. 123-1 et seq. (Trade and Companies Register), and R. 123-53 et seq. (registration particulars). SAS governance is principally set by its articles, subject to mandatory statutory rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent clerk of the commercial court (greffe du tribunal de commerce) maintains the Trade and Companies Register (Registre du commerce et des sociétés, RCS); applications are filed through the INPI-operated Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic application for registration in the RCS (demande d’immatriculation au RCS) submitted through the Guichet unique, supported by the signed SAS articles (statuts) and required evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid at incorporation; the balance must be paid within five years after registration. Cash contributions must be deposited before registration with an authorized depositary, such as a bank, notary, or the Caisse des dépôts et consignations, and a deposit certificate must be obtained. In-kind contributions are fully contributed at incorporation; an independent contribution auditor is generally required unless a statutory exemption applies. The USD filing-fee figure is an approximate conversion of the RCS registration charge; additional beneficial-owner filing, publication, and service charges may apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscriptions for the shares set out in the signed articles of association and acknowledges payment of the cash contributions evidenced by the deposit certificate. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [full French address], subject to any relocation procedure required by law and the articles. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed President (Président) for the term and on the terms provided in the articles, and that [name] is authorized to complete registration, tax, banking, and beneficial-owner formalities. The President is authorized to execute and submit all documents necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders; French notary where notarization is legally or transactionally required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles in French or provide a suitable French translation for filings. Specify the corporate name, purpose, registered office, duration, share capital, share rights, governance, President, and decision-making procedures. Have all founding shareholders sign. Notarization is not generally required for ordinary SAS articles; use a notarial deed where required for a contributed asset or other transaction.
required_dossiers: Description and valuation documentation for any in-kind contributions
Auditor report on in-kind contributions or documented basis for a statutory exemption, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies or missing mandatory particulars, obtain required signatures or contribution-auditor documentation, and execute amended articles before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital-deposit account and transfer the subscribed cash contributions. Obtain the deposit certificate identifying the company under formation, subscribers, and deposited amount. Ensure at least 50% of subscribed cash capital is paid before registration and retain evidence for the registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Proof of source of funds where requested under AML procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the depositary’s compliance queries with verified beneficial-owner, identity, and source-of-funds evidence; correct the subscription or transfer record before seeking the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal-announcement publication service in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the statutory incorporation notice after execution of the articles. Ensure it states the company name and form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, President’s identity, and registration venue. Obtain the publication certificate for the filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected or supplemental notice and obtain an updated publication certificate if required particulars are omitted or inaccurate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation and beneficial-owner declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises; competent commercial-court clerk for RCS registration and beneficial-owner processing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic RCS registration application through the Guichet unique. Upload the signed articles, registered-office evidence, publication certificate, capital-deposit certificate, President’s appointment and acceptance, identity and non-conviction declarations where applicable, and beneficial-owner information. Pay applicable filing charges and monitor the electronic dossier.
required_dossiers: President’s identity, acceptance, and required declarations
Translations or legalized/apostilled foreign documents where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer any clerk’s request for regularization through the Guichet unique by the stated deadline, upload corrected or missing documents, and pay any additional charge. Seek review or appeal through the competent registry procedure if registration is refused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, competent tax authorities, and the company’s depositary bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain and verify the SIREN/SIRET identifiers and Kbis extract, confirm publication and beneficial-owner registration, and provide the registration evidence to the bank to release the capital. Register for applicable tax and social-security processes and preserve corporate books and records.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct activity, address, or officer data through the Guichet unique; request registry correction for an erroneous extract and complete any outstanding tax or social-security registrations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to a France-based SAS conducting only ownership and cross-border sub-licensing of trademarks and patents. If the company later operates a regulated industrial facility, the competent authority is generally the Prefect, with technical review by the Regional Directorate for Environment, Planning and Housing (DREAL).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific manufacturing or operating license is ordinarily required for a pure intellectual-property holding and licensing business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition (Ministère de la Transition écologique); environmental review is administered by the competent environmental authority, generally the Prefect, with DREAL support.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not applicable to a pure IP holding and licensing activity with no relevant physical project or installation. A later project listed under the Environmental Code may require case-by-case screening or a full environmental impact assessment under Articles L. 122-1 and R. 122-2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No activity-specific discharge or emissions limits arise solely from IP ownership or licensing. If premises or operations generate regulated discharges, emissions, or waste, applicable Environmental Code and ICPE requirements, permit conditions, and waste-management rules apply; thresholds depend on the actual installation and pollutants.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial fire, structural-load, or occupational operating clearance is ordinarily required solely for a non-industrial IP company. Any occupied premises must comply with applicable building, fire-safety, and workplace health and safety rules; premises open to the public may require ERP authorization and fire-safety review, and industrial installations may require ICPE approvals.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), France - the online portal is impots.gouv.fr; for corporate tax and VAT registration, the relevant local office is the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) and for non-residents the Direction des résidents à l’étranger et des services généraux (DRESG).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity creating a French SAS must apply for a French tax identification number (numéro d’identification) through the DGFiP business formalities portal ('Formalités En Ligne' / guichet-entreprises.fr). For VAT purposes, the SAS obtains a French intra-community VAT number from the SIE upon submission of the bylaws, proof of registration at the RCS (extrait Kbis), proof of registered office or designated fiscal representative (for non-EU principals), identity documents of the legal representative, and a copy of the share capital evidence. A non-EU entity without a French permanent establishment must appoint a fiscal representative approved by the DGFiP for VAT and tax filings. The SIE then issues a TIN letter ('Avis de situation') and an EORI number where customs activities are anticipated.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - an SAS is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at the standard 25% rate and to VAT as a taxable person in France. The entity is within the territorial scope of French tax on its French-source and worldwide income as determined by article 209 of the French General Tax Code (CGI). The SAS cannot benefit from pass-through taxation except in narrow statutory exceptions not applicable to a trading IP HoldCo; however, the parent-subsidiary regime (article 145 CGI) and French tax consolidation (article 223 A CGI) are available at the entity level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a check-the-box election. Available elections relevant to an IP HoldCo include: election into the French VAT group (assujetti unique) under article 256 C III of the CGI; option for simplified or actual VAT settlement regimes under articles 287 and 287-0; election for VAT payment based on proceeds collected rather than invoiced (article 269); option for capital gains rollover relief under article 238 quindecies on IP transfers; election under EU ATAD 2 hybrid mismatch provisions (article 212 bis CGI) to neutralize or disallow deduction/non-inclusion mismatches; and election for the tax neutrality treatment of certain intangible contributions under article 210 A CGI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (French Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established SAS, there is no fixed VAT registration threshold; VAT applies from the first taxable transaction. The 'franchise en base de TVA' exemption is available only to small enterprises with an annual turnover of EUR 85,000 (principal sales of goods) or EUR 37,500 (services), and such businesses may opt for real VAT payment. A non-resident supplier with no establishment in France is required to register from the first French supply unless the transaction is covered by the OSS/IOSS scheme; the intra-EU distance sales threshold is EUR 10,000 for total cross-border supplies of goods and services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing a mandatory B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting regime under the 2023 Finance Act. From 1 September 2026, all taxable persons must be able to receive electronic invoices through a registered identity provider or through the public PPF (Portail Public de Facturation); from 1 September 2027, all taxable persons must issue and transmit e-invoices and transaction data to a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP). The reform imposes structured invoice data (Factur-X or cross-industry invoice formats) and continuous digital audit (via Fichier des Écritures Comptables) under article 289 bis CGI. There is no pre-clearance or digital stamping for standard invoices, but all invoices are subject to real-time or near-real-time transmission obligations once the platform is engaged.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under article 262-I-1° CGI applies to supplies of goods physically exported outside the European Union by or on behalf of the supplier. For an IP licensing enterprise, zero-rating is available for cross-border licensing and assignment of patents, trademarks, and underlying intangible rights supplied to a non-French customer under article 262-I-2° CGI, provided the place of supply is not in France under articles 259 A, 259 B, and 259 C CGI, and the recipient is a taxable person established outside the EU. The licensor must hold documentary evidence that the intellectual property rights are legally enforceable in the destination country and that the actual use and exploitation of the IP occurs outside France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU - Document Administratif Unique) or an EXL electronic export declaration for goods exports
Bill of Lading, CMR road consignment note, or air waybill evidencing physical movement of goods outside the EU
Commercial invoice issued by the French SAS
Customs exit proof validated by French customs or the customs office of exit from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/bank transfer reference showing payment in foreign currency from the non-resident licensee
Signed patent/trademark license agreement, proof of IP ownership/registration (INPI records), and a rationale demonstrating the place of actual IP use outside France
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP applies strict audit scrutiny on export zero-rating claims. Where the 0% VAT rate has been improperly claimed, the tax authority assesses the unpaid VAT plus late payment interest at 0.20% per month. The French Tax Procedure Code (LPF) allows law adjustment within the normal limitation period ending on 31 December of the third year following the relevant tax year, extended to six years in cases of hidden activity or tax fraud. Penalties are 40% for gross negligence (manquement délibéré) and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or carousel-type abuse (mauvaise foi); criminal tax fraud under article 1741 CGI carries imprisonment up to three years (five years if aggravated) and fines up to EUR 75,000 (EUR 500,000 for certain cross-border VAT fraud). In addition, customs law penalties may apply to missing export evidence or false declarations, including VAT reassessment and confiscation of reimbursements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as attached prudential supervisor and the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) as the foreign-exchange and balance-of-payments authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a euro-area member: the euro is fully convertible and capital movements are liberalised under Article 63 TFEU and Articles L151-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are free from exchange-control approval. Royalty inflows from foreign sub-licensees and dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are not exchange-controlled, but the intermediary French bank must perform the statutory balance-of-payments declaration to the Banque de France for cross-border settlements above €75,000 (Article R152-8 CMF) with monthly aggregate reporting and underlying invoices retained for five years. Dividend remittances may attract French withholding tax at 30% or a reduced treaty/Parent-Subsidiary rate; royalty payments to non-resident licensors may attract withholding tax under Article 182 B CGI with treaty relief, yet neither event requires central-bank authorisation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable and not imposed in France. There is no statutory surrender obligation, no repatriation window and no mandatory conversion ratio for export or licensing proceeds; the SAS may freely retain and convert foreign-currency receipts at market rates. The only mandatory compliance is the Banque de France statistical cross-border settlement declaration where the monthly transaction value reaches €75,000, which is filed by the collecting French bank on the company's behalf, and the company must maintain the underlying licence contracts, royalty statements and transfer-pricing documentation as evidence of economic substance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Operational Account with FX multi-currency sub-accounts
Operational Account with EUR/USD/GBP current accounts and treasury management line
Operational Account and Trade/LC facility; regional bank escrow possible

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE Group (Banque Populaire / Caisse d'Epargne with Natixis wholesale)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with e-banking treasury and hedging line
Operational Account and euro inbound collection account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for operational disbursement accounts, Low as a full-service master treasury bank. An EU-authorised Electronic Money Institution or payment institution passporting into France (e.g., a French PSD2-licensed EMI or a Luxembourg/German EMI using the single passport) may lawfully hold safeguarded client funds and process SEPA and SWIFT-style royalty transfers. However, such institutions cannot grant credit, cannot open a capital-escrow account in the same legal form as a credit institution, are not covered by the French FGDR deposit guarantee on the same terms, and generally cannot provide contracted FX forward/swap lines or documentary credit facilities. The SAS should therefore use a tier-1 credit institution as the master treasury bank and engage an EMI only for a segregated disbursement channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not universally mandate physical appearance: Articles L561-5 to L561-7 of the Code monétaire et financier and ACPR guidance permit secure remote identity verification via videoconference with identity-document validation and liveness detection. In panel practice, tier-1 banks require the SAS legal representative (Président) and all beneficial owners holding more than 25% to attend either an in-person interview at a branch or an approved video interview with certified identity extracts; for non-EEA resident owners, apostilled identity documents or a physical visit is still commonly required. The company must produce a current RCS/RNE extract (extrait Kbis or the new RNE extract) and the filed registre des bénéficiaires effectifs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain or non-EEA holding company in a low-substance or tax-haven jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Filing certificate of the French registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; group structure chart with percentage ownership; passport and proof of address of each natural-person owner; certified corporate excerpt and good-standing certificate of each intermediate holding company; signed source-of-wealth statement; transfer-pricing policy and a substance narrative describing the French licensing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty flows and business model indicative of a mailbox company with no operational substance in France
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current RCS/RNE extract; office lease or co-working agreement; payroll records of French employees; board minutes approving the IP licensing strategy and treasury policy; INPI/EPO/WIPO patent and trademark registration certificates; active IP-management evidence; French tax identifiers and attestation de résidence fiscale (form 5059).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentration of receipts from high-risk jurisdictions or parties on the EU/FATF non-cooperative lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly executed and audited sub-licence agreements; royalty calculation schedules; IP registration evidence; completed counterparty AML questionnaires; sanctions and country-risk screening matrix; invoices evidencing the French or treaty withholding-tax treatment of each payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-opening funds, third-party credit, or shareholder advances remitted before the bank relationship is established
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital-subscription resolution and blocked-account attestation (attestation du dépositaire des fonds) issued by a French bank or notary; accountant-certified ledger of accrued royalties; underlying licence or option agreements; source-of-fund declarations; signed treasury or cash-pool agreement documenting the character of any pre-opening shareholder funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound royalty receipt followed by a concentrated onward disbursement to offshore counterparties (layering pattern)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy and payment matrix; signed intercompany sub-licence or distribution agreements for onward flows; French transfer-pricing documentation under Article 57 CGI; written economic rationale for the onward payments; Banque de France reporting records for the settled transactions; and evidence of compliance with EU/OFAC sanctions screening by the French intermediary bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Pre-registration equity capital is deposited in a French bank blocked account (compte bloqué) in the name of the future SAS; the depositary issues an attestation de blocage and the funds are released to the operating account upon RCS registration. Post-incorporation equity or shareholder-loan injections are received by SWIFT MT103 with purpose code CAPC (or the equivalent bank remittance code) referencing the extraordinary general meeting resolution and the French registration number. Inbound royalty collections from EEA sub-licensees are cleared by SEPA Credit Transfer using the ISO 20022 purpose code ROYA (royalties) or LIC (licence fees); non-EEA and non-EUR receipts use SWIFT MT103 with field 70 stating the licence agreement reference, patent or trademark registration number, royalty period and amount, and, where French VAT is chargeable, the matching VAT invoice or reverse-charge reference. The receiving French bank generates the Banque de France statistical declaration for monthly cross-border settlements at or above the €75,000 threshold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Euro disbursements to EEA beneficiaries use SEPA Credit Transfer (standard or instant) with full remittance information. Non-EEA and non-euro disbursements are executed by SWIFT MT103 through the French bank correspondent network with complete beneficiary identification in field 59 and the applicable purpose code LIC or ROYA. Where the SAS secures a counterparty's payment obligation or conditions a milestone payment under a patent acquisition, a Commercial Letter of Credit may be issued under UCP 600 via MT700, or a Standby Letter of Credit may be accepted as collateral. Euro legs clear through TARGET2/Euro1 using the bank's BIC; non-euro legs clear over SWIFT with standard value dating (typically T+2 for USD). Every payment order is screened against EU/OFAC sanctions, and the ledger must support the Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration and the five-year record-keeping obligation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forward (change à terme) with an ACPR-licensed credit institution
Rolling FX forward (change à terme renouvelable) for annual rolling royalty hedges
FX swap (swap de change) on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF or EUR/JPY for short-term liquidity conversion
Cross-currency swap (swap de devises) transforming intercompany loan interest and principal into the desired invoice currency
Vanilla FX option or tunnel/collar structure to cap hedging cost and secure a budget rate
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for restricted-convertibility or exotic currencies used by emerging-market sub-licensees, subject to EMIR margin, clearing and counterparty-limit obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts, including statutory management report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce) through the Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after the financial year-end and filed within one month after approval; electronic filing is generally permitted within two months after approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in a court injunction, a civil fine of up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance, and potential registry enforcement measures. Administrative strike-off is not triggered automatically by a single missed filing but may follow formal notices and continuing inactivity or non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after the financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company, unless a specific extension applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, interest for late payment, and additional penalties for persistent or materially incorrect reporting. Tax administration enforcement may include assessments, audits, and collection proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual confirmation is required solely because a new year begins. Changes to beneficial ownership or control must generally be reported within 30 days of the change; an update may also be required upon registry request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate beneficial ownership information may result in formal notice, criminal sanctions for responsible persons, and restrictions or enforcement concerning the company's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder and corporate decision documentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No routine filing authority; documents are maintained at the registered office and made available to competent authorities or shareholders where legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual ordinary shareholder approval should occur within six months after the financial year-end unless extended by court order.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or document required decisions may expose the company and officers to court orders, liability claims, accounting-filing consequences, and defects in corporate approvals.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of three thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet assets, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 employees. Mandatory appointment may also arise for qualifying control or group relationships, or by court order upon a qualifying shareholder request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority framework apply to statutory individual accounts. IFRS is generally relevant to qualifying consolidated accounts where legally permitted or required, not as the default framework for SAS statutory individual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation merely because the company completes another financial year. The company must continuously maintain accurate control information and file changes generally within 30 days. Share transfers must be recorded in the securities movement register and individual shareholder securities accounts, with corresponding UBO analysis and filing where control changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register or file of shareholder decisions and minutes
Register or file of decisions of the president and other corporate bodies
Beneficial ownership filing records and supporting control documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 600-1,800 per year, depending on location, mail handling, administrative support, and document forwarding services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-15,000 per year for a qualifying SAS, depending on turnover, group reporting, transaction complexity, and audit scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.00% (standard rate for fiscal years beginning on/after 1 January 2022; plus a 3.3% social surcharge on the corporate income tax amount where the company satisfies the turnover and tax thresholds, bringing the effective marginal rate to approximately 25.83%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying small enterprises with turnover below EUR 10,000,000; preferential 10% patent/innovation box rate on qualifying net patent licensing income (Article 238 CGI, OECD nexus ratio required); Research Tax Credit (CIR) of 30% on eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100,000,000 and 5% above that threshold; 95% participation-exemption regime for qualifying dividends from EU/non-EU subsidiaries; no notional interest deduction regime.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_regime_notes: France permits indefinite carryforward of tax losses (report en avant) under Article 209 CGI, but the annual offset is limited to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000; losses may alternatively be carried back (report en arrière) for a maximum of 3 years and capped at EUR 1,000,000, generally creating a tax credit refundable after 5 years.
